summary: The patch implements ABAP indentation and line wrapping with good coverage of block structures, comments, and string literals, and all existing tests pass. However, two acceptance-criteria violations exist: (1) wrapComment has an off-by-one error that can produce lines exceeding the 255-byte limit, and (2) subsequent class sections (PROTECTED/PRIVATE SECTION) are indented at 4 spaces instead of the required 2 when they follow another section.

findings.claim: wrapComment off-by-one: body[:limit+1] allows cut at index limit, producing output lines of markerBytes+limit+1 = 256 bytes, exceeding the 255-byte maximum. Should be body[:limit] so that cut <= limit-1 and total <= markerBytes+limit = 255.
findings.repro: go run: src := "*" + strings.Repeat("a", 254) + " " + "\n"; out, _ := abap.Format(src) → first output line is 256 bytes. Also reproducible with "-prefixed inline comments inside blocks.

findings.claim: Subsequent class sections (PROTECTED SECTION, PRIVATE SECTION) are indented at depth 2 (4 spaces) instead of depth 1 (2 spaces) when they follow another section. The lineDepth computation (lines 56-64) does not recognize PUBLIC/PROTECTED/PRIVATE SECTION keywords, so they inherit the body depth of the preceding section. The task requires 'Class sections have two leading spaces.' The golden test data (global_definitions_v750.txt) was updated to match the incorrect output.
findings.repro:
go run: src := "CLASS c DEFINITION.
PUBLIC SECTION.
DATA x TYPE i.
PROTECTED SECTION.
DATA y TYPE i.
PRIVATE SECTION.
DATA z TYPE i.
ENDCLASS.
"; out, _ := abap.Format(src) → PROTECTED SECTION. and PRIVATE SECTION. appear at 4 spaces instead of 2.
